sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Turkmenistan.
Turkmenistan is a dry, desert,
and historic country in Central Asia.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Turkmenistan?
Turkmenistan is in Central Asia.
It is next to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan,
Afghanistan, and Iran.
To the west, it touches the Caspian Sea.
It has deserts, mountains, and oases.
What is the capital city of Turkmenistan?
The capital city is Ashgabat.
Ashgabat has white buildings, large parks, and wide streets.
It is known for its marble architecture and statues.
It is the largest city in the country.
Other cities include Turkmenabad and Old Trade Center,
Dashoguz in the north,
Mary near ancient ruins,
Balkanabad in the west.
How many people live in Turkmenistan?
About 6.5 million people live in Turkmenistan.
Many people live in cities,
but others live in small towns or rural areas.
What language do people speak in Turkmenistan?
The official language is Turkmen.
Many people also speak Russian, especially older adults.
Some people speak Uzbek, Kazakh, or Persian in some regions.
What is the weather like in Turkmenistan?
Turkmenistan has a desert climate.
Hot and dry summers,
sometimes over 40 degrees Celsius.
Cold winters, especially in the north.
Little rain during the year.
Sandstorms happen in the desert.
It is one of the driest countries in Central Asia.
What does Turkmenistan look like?
Turkmenistan has the Karakum Desert
covering most of the land mountains in the south,
the Caspian Sea in the west,
Green Valley's near rivers,
the Darvaza Gas Crater,
also called the door to hell.
It has many natural and unusual landscapes.
What animals live in Turkmenistan?
Turkmenistan is home to camels, sheep, and horses,
foxes, wolves, and gazelles,
eagles, owls, and snakes,
desert lizards and insects.
The Akalteke horse is a national symbol
and known for its speed and beauty.
What do people eat in Turkmenistan?
Turkmen food is simple, meaty, and traditional.
People eat bread, flatbread, called chorak,
rice, noodles, and wheat dishes,
lamb, beef, and chicken,
onions, carrots, and melons,
popular dishes,
plav, rice with meat and carrots,
shashlik, grilled meat on sticks,
mantis, steamed dumplings,
dograma soup with lamb and bread,
gawarma, fried meat, and fat for storage.
Melons from Turkmenistan are famous and very sweet.
What do people drink in Turkmenistan?
People drink green tea with almost every meal.
Water, very important in the desert.
Fermented milk, chow, fruit juice,
like melon or grape.
Adults may drink local wine or vodka,
though alcohol is less common.
Tea is a symbol of hospitality and respect.
What is life like in Turkmenistan?
Life is often quiet, traditional, and community-based.
People enjoy spending time with family,
drinking tea and talking,
wearing traditional clothes,
taking care of animals,
celebrating weddings and holidays.
Many people live in simple homes
and follow old customs.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, September 27,
Nauru Spring Festival,
March 24th, Edao and Edao Ada.
Melon Day in August,
horse day celebrating the Akal Teque horse.
People celebrate with food, music,
dancing, and colorful clothing.
Some fun facts about Turkmenistan.
The Darvaza gas crater has burned for over 50 years.
The Akal Teque horse is one of the oldest horse breeds.
Ashkabat holds a world record
for the most white marble buildings.
Turkmen carpets are handmade and very beautiful.
The flag has green, red, and a rug design
with a crescent moon and stars.
Now you know many things about Turkmenistan.
You know where it is,
what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the desert,
tea, and traditions.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
